findings.evidence: Bundle KC: ‘use dot-and-cross diagrams to illustrate ionic, covalent and coordinate bonding including the representation of any compounds stated in 3.4 and 3.5’. Pack item 9701-3.7-i01 asks ‘Identify the correct outer-shell dot-and-cross representation of MgO.’ The chapter questions ask learners to identify/select/count features, but none asks them to draw or construct a dot-and-cross diagram for any of the three bonding types.
findings.suggested: Add at least one question requiring learners to draw dot-and-cross diagrams for ionic, covalent and coordinate bonding, including a compound from 3.4/3.5.
findings.resolution: fix: The finding is valid: recognition/counting items do not assess construction of dot-and-cross diagrams required by procedural KC 9701-3.7.1. Replace generated item 9701-3.7-i01 in full with the following exact object (remove its old options, answer, distractors and shuffle fields); retain all other items. NH3 and NH4+ are explicitly included in bundle 3.4, and NH3 is also in 3.5. This is a generated marking scheme, not an official past-paper scheme. For (a), use dots for electrons originally from O and crosses for electrons originally from Mg; omit inner shells and show no electrons on Mg2+. For (b) and (c), use dots for electrons originally from N and crosses for electrons originally from H. Include all lone pairs and any required brackets and charges.", "marks": 6, "scheme": [{"mark": "B1", "point": "(a) Separate bracketed Mg and O ions with charges 2+ and 2− respectively; no shared pair between the ions."}, {"mark": "B1", "point": "(a) Eight electrons around O: six dots originally from O and two crosses transferred from Mg; omit inner shells and show no electrons on Mg."}, {"mark": "B1", "point": "(b) Three N–H shared pairs, each containing one dot from N and one cross from H."}, {"mark": "B1", "point": "(b) One lone pair of two dots on N, no further electrons and no ionic charge."}, {"mark": "B1", "point": "(c) Four N–H shared pairs: three dot–cross pairs and one dot–dot pair donated by N to the incoming H+; no lone pair remains on N."}, {"mark": "B1", "point": "(c) Enclose the whole NH4+ ion in brackets with an overall + charge; show no additional electrons."}], "explanation": "MgO contains separate Mg2+ and O2− ions after transfer of two electrons from Mg to O. NH3 has three shared N–H pairs and one nitrogen lone pair; donation of that lone pair to H+ forms a fourth shared pair in NH4+, leaving no nitrogen lone pair and an overall + charge. The dot–dot pair records the origin of the coordinate pair; all four N–H bonds are equivalent after formation.", "hints": ["Start by identifying the atoms and the electrons they originally supply.", "Distinguish electron transfer from electron sharing, and track the origin of each electron.", "Write the neutral-atom valence counts for Mg, O, N and H before arranging the electrons; H+ contributes no electron."]}
